title: Epigenetic entropy, socioeconomic differences, and health and lifespan in the Women's Health Initiative.
authors: Mozhui, Khyobeni; Starlard-Davenport, Athena; Sun, Yangbo; Shadyab, Aladdin H; Casanova, Ramon; Thomas, Fridtjof; Wallace, Robert B; Fowke, Jay H; Johnson, Karen C
one_liner_zh: 该研究基于DNA甲基化数据计算表观遗传熵，分析社会经济差异与健康寿命的关联，属于纯表观遗传统计与流行病学分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模、无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aging is marked by changes in DNA methylation (DNAm) including an increase in randomness or entropy in the epigenome. Here, we computed epigenetic entropy using DNAm data from the Women's Health Initiative (WHI) ancillary study AS315 (n = 2192), and tested for replication in WHI ancillary studies, BA23 (n = 1989) and AS311 (n = 868). We investigated how different metrics of epigenetic stochasticity relate to demographic variables, health, and mortality risk, and how these compare to machine-learning based models of aging such as the DunedinPACE. RESULTS: Epigenetic entropy had robust and consistent negative associations with income and education in the WHI. Notably, low income was related to increased stochasticity and higher methylation in DNA regions that are targeted by the polycomb proteins-key regulators of cellular memory and embryonic development. While higher income was associated with reduced entropy scores and lower DunedinPACE in White women, this effect of income was diminished in Black and Hispanic women, and on average, Black and Hispanic women had relatively higher stochastic variability. Painting a complex picture, our analysis of the polycomb regions in a small cohort of children showed significant positive associations with parental income. Additionally, in the WHI, higher DunedinPACE predicted higher mortality risk, while the maintenance of methylation at enhancer regions was associated with improved survival. CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate close ties between social and economic factors and aspects of epigenetic aging, and highlight the polycomb targeted CpGs as potential sensors of the social environment and related exposures across demographic groups.
abstract_zh: 背景：衰老的特征包括DNA甲基化（DNAm）的变化，如表观基因组中随机性或熵的增加。在此，我们利用妇女健康倡议（WHI）辅助研究AS315（n = 2192）的DNAm数据计算了表观遗传熵，并在WHI辅助研究BA23（n = 1989）和AS311（n = 868）中进行了复制验证。我们研究了表观遗传随机性的不同指标如何与人口统计学变量、健康和死亡风险相关，以及这些指标与基于机器学习的衰老模型（如DunedinPACE）的比较。结果：在WHI中，表观遗传熵与收入和受教育程度具有稳健且一致的负相关。值得注意的是，低收入与随机性增加以及多梳蛋白（polycomb proteins）靶向的DNA区域中甲基化水平升高相关，而多梳蛋白是细胞记忆和胚胎发育的关键调控因子。虽然较高收入与白人女性中熵评分降低和DunedinPACE较低相关，但这种收入效应在黑人及西班牙裔女性中减弱，且平均而言，黑人及西班牙裔女性具有相对较高的随机变异性。为呈现复杂图景，我们对一个小型儿童队列中多梳区域的分析显示，其与父母收入存在显著正相关。此外，在WHI中，较高的DunedinPACE预测了更高的死亡风险，而增强子区域甲基化的维持与生存率提高相关。结论：这些发现表明社会经济因素与表观遗传衰老的各个方面之间存在密切联系，并强调多梳靶向CpG位点可能作为不同人口群体中社会环境及相关暴露的潜在传感器。
